correctness.rationale: For diagonal matrices the pivot update zeros precisely the sampled weight; exponential clocks reproduce the sequential probabilities. Conditional on the last high clock the count is binomial, yielding the finite PGF/PMF by its Laplace transform. With a=lambda*n, fixed-r conditional Poisson mixing factors into independent geometric PGFs. For r->infinity and r=o(n), the high maximum has mean H_r and bounded variance, and conditional binomial fluctuations give the exact Gaussian window; the conditional mean differs from mu_n by only O_p(1). The trace-error event is exactly full high-coordinate capture because a-1>epsilon(n-r)+s in the stated regime. The standalone rational checker compared an independent Markov recursion and the closed forms in 1383 checks. Finitary experiments are only checks, not universal proofs.

value.rationale: The result answers a natural accuracy-budget question for residual-weighted pivoted Cholesky that universal expected trace bounds do not quantify sharply: how many extra columns make all dominant spectral coordinates appear with high probability? The exact finite stopping distribution and Gaussian transition quantify that cost on the benchmark two-plateau family, distinguish O(log r) oversampling from the worst-case O(r/epsilon) scale, and identify that binomial fluctuations dominate the Gumbel maximum-clock randomness. It is a deliberately bounded structured benchmark, not a universal kernel theorem.
